transcript.text: Agility is the newest skill in RuneScape Dragon Wilds and it's also one of the most important skills to level early on.
But, just like every skill in RuneScape, leveling it up is going to take some grinding and even on a custom server
with three times XP, it would still take you a very long time to reach level 99 and unlock every spell, ability, and
perk that this skill has to offer. But, agility is definitely worth leveling up as soon as possible and in this video,
I'll cover why you should actually level it, what you'll unlock along the way, and what the best tips are to level your
agility as fast as possible. The first thing to know is why you want to start training your agility as early as
possible. The agility tree will not only reduce the stamina drain of sprinting, but it also unlocks many useful ability
perks and spells that will help you traverse the world much, much easier. You can only gain agility XP through
running around the world on foot as moving around with your mount will not grant any XP at all. There are plenty in
the world where your mount is not really allowed at all or you are in combat and simply can't do so. So, having extra
movement and more stamina really can make all of the difference when you're fighting some of the more difficult
bosses. It also gives you access to a special teleport network that I will cover in a bit more detail later on and
it provides you with some cool cosmetic skill capes if you're able to complete each agility course in the gold time
frame. Now, I just wanted to quickly go over the abilities and perks that you will unlock throughout the agility skill
tree starting with the non-special skill points which reduce the stamina drain of sprinting by 0.085%
per level until you reach level 99 and it caps out at 8.415%. When it comes to your unlocks at level
five, you'll unlock Wind Step which allows you release an air blast below your feet so that you can jump up to
higher places. At level 10, you'll get the double jump ability, allowing you to jump a second time when in the air.
At level 22, you get hopper, which reduces the stamina cost of jumping. At level 32, you'll unlock air dash,
which allows you to dash horizontally in the air in order to evade attacks in combat.
At level 35, you'll get break fall, which automatically allows you to roll when hitting the ground, reducing your
fall damage. At level 40, you'll get wind stomp, which staggers nearby enemies when landing from a wind step.
At level 44, you'll get phase dash, which allows you to dash a second time while airborne.
At level 48, you'll unlock nomad, which simply increases the passive experience you gain while exploring the world. At
level 50, you'll get backpacker, increasing your max carry weight by 75 additional pounds. At level 53, you'll
unlock the stamina potion, which can be used to stop stamina drain while running. At level 54, you'll get greater break
fall, which further reduces fall damage. At level 57, you'll get recall, which leaves a runic marker on the ground that
you can recast to teleport back to in the middle of combat or a dangerous situation.
At level 70, you'll get reactive recall, which allows your recall ability to now automatically trigger upon receiving
fatal damage, protecting you from at least one fatal hit. At level 75, you'll get explorer, increasing your max carry
weight by another 75 pounds. At level 85, you'll get trailblazer, which increases the amount of passive XP
you'll continue to get all the way up until eventually level 99, where you'll unlock the ever infamous agility skill
cape. Now, I wanted to cover the agility courses that you'll be unlocking throughout your play through and what
kind of rewards you should be expecting. The first one you will have access to is
at level one and it's called chasm dash. It is located here in Brynn Mor, near one of the first vaults. This one does
not have any perk requirements and is fairly simple to navigate. If you're able to get the gold time, you will be
awarded with a gold medal to hang on your wall as well as the region's skill cape on first-time completion. After
that, each subsequent run you'll be rewarded either with a gold, silver, or bronze pack that just has some rune
seeds, gems, or bait from that specific zone as well as feathers and leaves that will be used to craft various agility
items. Next up is the Fractured Ruins trial, which is located here in the Fractured Plains biome and requires
level 15 agility because you will need to be using wind step and double jump in order to clear it. This one took a few
tries to get the timing for [music] on the wind step, but if you're able to clear it on gold time, you'll be awarded
a medal once again and another region-specific skill cape. After that is the Thunder Assault located here in
the Stormtouched Highlands. This one again requires level 15 agility because you'll be using wind step and double
jump, so make sure you have it before going out there. A gold time will once again reward a medal and a skill cape.
And just to note, this trial and the previous one will both reward the same Gornfell packs, so farm whichever one
you think is easier after you beat them for the fastest time. Then you will want to head over to Fell Hollow and take on
the Grave Run trial located here. This one requires level 30 agility and requires you to have a bit more skill
when it comes [music] to actually navigating narrow beams floating high inside of the air. But once you unlock
the gold time here, you'll get another medal and a pretty cool-looking skill cape to go with it. Every run after will
just give Fell Hollow packs, so if you need those gems or more importantly power level five ascension shards, these
will have a 25% chance to drop them. Next will be the Tower Climb, which is located here in Dowden Reach. This
course currently requires 51 agility because you will now need to use the air dash in order to complete it in the
fastest possible time. Once you get the route down on this one, it's pretty easy to get a gold time, and it's also easy
to just jump off and start over if you're having a bad run or simply mess up your run along the way. So, for
farming purposes, this one is actually pretty decent. The rewards, the skill cape, the metal, and the gold packs have
a chance to drop a power level six ascension shard, as well as some leaves and various gemstones. Finally, will be
the Lava Fields trial located inside the Umbral Sands biome. This trial requires
level 65 agility, and just requires that the you have double jump and air dash. The trial has tons of different fire and
some tricky timing on the jump puzzles, but once you get the gold time here for the very first time, you will once again
get the metal and the skill cape. The packs here can drop power level seven ascension shard, the Garochit, Garu
artifacts, as well as leaves and gems once again to help you out. Once you've completed the skill courses, you will
have a good stock pile of feathers as well as leaves that you can use to craft some very useful agility items. The
warped feathers will be used to craft the Gyre Hawk amulet, which grants a whopping 100% agility EXP gain from
exploration. Leaves that you'll also gather from the agility course packs will be used to craft your agility XP
potions, and the gold leaves can be used to craft the gilded Gyre Hawk amulet, which now consumes warped feathers to
keep the previous 100% XP buff, and also gives you an additional 25% XP from agility courses. I just wanted to also
briefly go over the Kibble Holes for you that you'll start to gain access to as you level up your agility. These are
scattered all over the map and must be dug up with a shovel in order to actually unlock them. Once you find your
first two, a network will become available, showing you each point that you can travel to on the map using the
burrows. Leveling up your agility will grant you access to higher tiered zones and the final burrows in the Umbral
Sands biome will be unlocked at level 67. You will also take a small amount of damage when using these networks as a
kind of a drawback, but this is also reduced as you level up the skill with the final upgrade coming for this being
at level 80. Finally, I wanted to go over some leveling tips for agility to help you level up as quick as possible.
As mentioned earlier, agility EXP is earned from running around on foot, but you can also gain EXP from simply
rolling and dodging as well. The best tip I can tell you is that rolling through traps in the world as well as in
dungeons is by far the best method for farming experience right now. My personal favorite spot is probably here
in the Stormtouch Mountains Vault where you can find a spinning fire trap. Make sure that you have a decent amount of
food buffs with you as well as the knowledge's nourishment buff and your best agility potion. Either the lesser
that gives 15% XP or greater that gives 30% are both usable. If you are able to craft the inspiring ring of agility,
make sure that you also grab that as well. Once you find the trap, you will simply want to roll around in the fire
to power level your agility. If you do it just right, you can roll multiple times in place and stack the EXP like
crazy. Just make sure that you have the food prepared because the fire can get pretty hot along the way. I really only
suggest this method if you need to catch up in agility levels or after you have already completed all the agility
courses on gold since those give a massive chunk of experience for the first time that you complete them. But,
agility in Dragon Isles is much more enjoyable than it is in Old School, unlike woodcutting where it is just
going to be a grind either way. But, if you want to learn how to level up that skill as fast as possible, consider
checking out this video.
